primary_purpose: Variant quality assessment and filtering
input: Variant call files and pipeline metrics
output: Filtered and annotated VCFs; QC metrics
selection_rationale: Representative toolkit for variant quality assessment and filtering.
appropriate_use: Use with validated laboratory pipeline and documented filters.
interpretation_boundary: Not a substitute for case-level clinical interpretation.
key_limitations: Pipeline- and parameter-dependent.
supporting_citation: DePristo MA, Banks E, Poplin R, Garimella KV, Maguire JR, Hartl C, et al. A framework for variation discovery and genotyping using next-generation DNA sequencing data. Nat Genet. 2011;43(5):491-498. doi:10.1038/ng.806.

primary_purpose: Variant quality assessment and filtering
selection_rationale: Included as a lightweight, widely used option for normalization, filtering, and inspection of variant calls.
appropriate_use: Use when transparent VCF-level processing or normalization is required.
interpretation_boundary: Does not establish variant validity or pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Pipeline- and parameter-dependent.
supporting_citation: Danecek P, Bonfield JK, Liddle J, Marshall J, Ohan V, Pollard MO, et al. Twelve years of SAMtools and BCFtools. GigaScience. 2021;10(2):giab008. doi:10.1093/gigascience/giab008.

primary_purpose: Variant quality assessment and filtering
selection_rationale: Included for transparent VCF-level filtering and summary operations in variant quality assessment and filtering.
appropriate_use: Use for inspection, filtering, and cohort-level VCF summaries as appropriate.
interpretation_boundary: Does not replace validation of calls or clinical evidence appraisal.
key_limitations: Pipeline- and parameter-dependent. Maintenance is legacy; bcftools covers many of the same VCF operations.
supporting_citation: Danecek P, Auton A, Abecasis G, Albers CA, Banks E, DePristo MA, et al. The variant call format and VCFtools. Bioinformatics. 2011;27(15):2156-2158. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btr330.

primary_purpose: Variant, gene, and transcript annotation
selection_rationale: Included as a maintained reference ecosystem for genome, gene, transcript, and variant annotation.
appropriate_use: Use when annotation requires explicit genome-build and transcript context.
interpretation_boundary: Transcript annotations are not a clinical classification.
key_limitations: Transcript and genome-build discrepancies.
supporting_citation: Cunningham F, Allen JE, Allen J, Alvarez-Jarreta J, Amode MR, Armean IM, et al. Ensembl 2024. Nucleic Acids Res. 2024;52(D1):D891-D899. doi:10.1093/nar/gkad1049.

primary_purpose: Variant, gene, and transcript annotation
selection_rationale: Included as a core curated reference-sequence source for transcript-aware interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when documenting transcript accessions and reference sequence context.
interpretation_boundary: A transcript record alone does not determine disease relevance.
key_limitations: Transcript and genome-build discrepancies. Transcript updates and alternative isoforms require explicit selection.
supporting_citation: O’Leary NA, Wright MW, Brister JR, Ciufo S, Haddad D, McVeigh R, et al. Reference sequence (RefSeq) database at NCBI: current status, taxonomic expansion, and functional annotation. Nucleic Acids Res. 2016;44(D1):D733-D745. doi:10.1093/nar/gkv1189.

primary_purpose: Variant, gene, and transcript annotation
selection_rationale: Included because comprehensive annotation supports transparent transcript and gene context.
appropriate_use: Use when transcript-model provenance must be documented.
interpretation_boundary: Does not determine clinical transcript preference by itself.
key_limitations: Transcript and genome-build discrepancies.
supporting_citation: Frankish A, Diekhans M, Jungreis I, Lagarde J, Loveland JE, Mudge JM, et al. GENCODE 2021. Nucleic Acids Res. 2021;49(D1):D916-D923. doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa1087.

primary_purpose: Variant, gene, and transcript annotation
technical_compatibility: NCBI/Ensembl identifiers. GRCh37 coverage is not universal.
selection_rationale: Included to support consistent transcript selection across RefSeq and Ensembl for clinically relevant reporting.
appropriate_use: Use when a MANE transcript is available and appropriate to the clinical context.
interpretation_boundary: Does not eliminate the need to consider disease-specific transcript conventions.
key_limitations: Transcript and genome-build discrepancies. Coverage is not universal; updates occur over time.
supporting_citation: Morales J, Pujar S, Loveland JE, Astashyn A, Bennett R, Berry A, et al. A joint NCBI and EMBL-EBI transcript set for clinical genomics and research. Nature. 2022;604(7905):310-315. doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04558-8.

primary_purpose: Population frequency assessment and frequency-based filtering
selection_rationale: Included because large-scale population data can test compatibility of allele frequency with a suspected disease model.
appropriate_use: Use for frequency filtering and ancestry-aware contextual assessment.
interpretation_boundary: Rarity or absence does not establish pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Population representation and ancestry bias; rarity alone does not establish pathogenicity. Coverage differences, founder effects, and no phenotype linkage.
supporting_citation: Gudmundsson S, Singer-Berk M, Watts NA, Phu W, Goodrich JK, Solomonson M, et al. Variant interpretation using population databases: lessons from gnomAD. Hum Mutat. 2022;43(8):1012-1030. doi:10.1002/humu.24309.

primary_purpose: Population frequency assessment and frequency-based filtering
technical_compatibility: Public allele-frequency browser (Bravo). Program description: https://topmed.nhlbi.nih.gov/. Controlled-access freezes are distinct from the public browser. GRCh37 availability depends on the release.
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary large-scale frequency resource. The catalogued URL is the public Bravo browser of TOPMed allele frequencies.
appropriate_use: Use when its cohort composition and release are relevant to the frequency question.
interpretation_boundary: Frequency alone is not clinical evidence of pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Population representation and ancestry bias; rarity alone does not establish pathogenicity.
supporting_citation: Taliun D, Harris DN, Kessler MD, Carlson J, Szpiech ZA, Torres R, et al. Sequencing of 53,831 diverse genomes from the NHLBI TOPMed Program. Nature. 2021;590(7845):290-299. doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03205-y.

primary_purpose: Population frequency assessment and frequency-based filtering
selection_rationale: Included as a foundational multi-population reference dataset for complementary frequency and ancestry context.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary context rather than sole frequency evidence.
interpretation_boundary: Does not establish pathogenicity or fully represent all populations.
key_limitations: Population representation and ancestry bias; rarity alone does not establish pathogenicity. Limited sample sizes for rare-variant inference relative to newer datasets.
supporting_citation: 1000 Genomes Project Consortium. A global reference for human genetic variation. Nature. 2015;526(7571):68-74. doi:10.1038/nature15393.

primary_purpose: Population frequency assessment and frequency-based filtering
selection_rationale: Included to provide population-relevant frequency context when patient ancestry is appropriately matched.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary evidence for appropriately matched Iranian cases.
interpretation_boundary: Should not be assumed to represent all Iranian or neighboring populations.
key_limitations: Population representation and ancestry bias; rarity alone does not establish pathogenicity.
supporting_citation: Fattahi Z, Beheshtian M, Mohseni M, Poustchi H, Sellars E, Nezhadi SH, et al. Iranome: a catalog of genomic variations in the Iranian population. Hum Mutat. 2019;40(11):1968-1984. doi:10.1002/humu.23880.

primary_purpose: Phenotype–gene matching and candidate prioritization
input: Clinical features encoded as HPO terms
output: Ontology terms and phenotype similarity context
selection_rationale: Included because structured phenotype encoding supports reproducible phenotype–gene and phenotype–disease comparison.
appropriate_use: Use when clinical findings can be captured with sufficiently specific and temporally appropriate terms.
interpretation_boundary: HPO is phenotype encoding. Phenotype similarity does not independently establish gene–disease causality or variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Incomplete, nonspecific, or inaccurately captured phenotypes.
supporting_citation: Köhler S, Gargano M, Matentzoglu N, Carmody LC, Lewis-Smith D, Vasilevsky NA, et al. The Human Phenotype Ontology in 2021. Nucleic Acids Res. 2021;49(D1):D1207-D1217. doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa1043.

primary_purpose: Phenotype–gene matching and candidate prioritization
input: HPO terms; variant data; pedigree where applicable
technical_compatibility: VCF plus phenotype inputs Documentation tracks application release 15.1.1; phenotype and genome data bundles are versioned separately.
selection_rationale: Included as a representative phenotype-driven prioritization platform that integrates phenotype and variant context.
appropriate_use: Use for candidate prioritization when structured phenotype and compatible variant data are available.
interpretation_boundary: Ranking is not proof of causality or classification.
key_limitations: Incomplete, nonspecific, or inaccurately captured phenotypes. Dependent on phenotype quality, knowledgebase coverage, inheritance assumptions, and model configuration.
supporting_citation: Smedley D, Jacobsen JOB, Jäger M, Köhler S, Holtgrewe M, Schubach M, et al. Next-generation diagnostics and disease-gene discovery with the Exomiser. Nat Protoc. 2015;10(12):2004-2015. doi:10.1038/nprot.2015.124.

primary_purpose: Phenotype–gene matching and candidate prioritization
input: HPO terms; genotype information when available
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary phenotype-driven method emphasizing explicit likelihood-based reasoning.
appropriate_use: Use when transparent phenotype-based diagnostic prioritization is desired.
interpretation_boundary: Output does not independently prove causal variant status.
key_limitations: Incomplete, nonspecific, or inaccurately captured phenotypes. Sensitive to phenotype completeness, disease annotations, and input assumptions.
supporting_citation: Robinson PN, Ravanmehr V, Jacobsen JOB, Danis D, Zhang H, Carmody LC, et al. Interpretable clinical genomics with a likelihood ratio paradigm. Am J Hum Genet. 2020;107(3):403-417. doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2020.06.021.

primary_purpose: Phenotype–gene matching and candidate prioritization
technical_compatibility: HPO term input; web/API where available
selection_rationale: Included as a focused phenotype-to-gene prioritization option.
appropriate_use: Use for rapid gene prioritization from structured phenotypes.
interpretation_boundary: Does not provide variant classification.
key_limitations: Incomplete, nonspecific, or inaccurately captured phenotypes. Limited by phenotype encoding and underlying gene–phenotype knowledge.
supporting_citation: Zhao M, Havrilla JM, Fang L, Chen Y, Peng J, Liu C, et al. Phen2Gene: rapid phenotype-driven gene prioritization for rare diseases. NAR Genom Bioinform. 2020;2(2):lqaa032. doi:10.1093/nargab/lqaa032.

primary_purpose: Assessment of gene–disease validity and clinical relevance; Retrieval and assessment of clinical and literature-based evidence; Clinical reporting, documentation, and reassessment
output: Curated gene–disease validity assertions and supporting evidence summaries
selection_rationale: Included because ClinGen expert curation supports gene–disease validity assessment and evidence review when a current assertion exists.
appropriate_use: Use for gene–disease validity and related curated evidence when current curation exists. Gene- and disease-specific classification specifications are the separate ClinGen specifications entry.
interpretation_boundary: Coverage is incomplete. A validity or evidence assertion does not classify the variant under review and does not replace case-specific appraisal.
key_limitations: Evidence is evolving and may vary in strength and curation status. Conflicting, heterogeneous, or incompletely curated evidence. Evidence and interpretations may change over time. This entry does not contain the gene-specific ACMG/AMP specifications, which are catalogued separately.
supporting_citation: Rehm HL, Berg JS, Brooks LD, Bustamante CD, Evans JP, Landrum MJ, et al. ClinGen—the Clinical Genome Resource. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(23):2235-2242. doi:10.1056/NEJMsr1406261.

primary_purpose: Assessment of gene–disease validity and clinical relevance
selection_rationale: Included as a widely used gene–phenotype knowledge source for evaluating clinical relevance.
appropriate_use: Use to contextualize known gene–disease relationships and inheritance patterns.
interpretation_boundary: Does not replace formal validity assessment or case-specific classification.
key_limitations: Evidence is evolving and may vary in strength and curation status. Curation depth and update timing vary by entry.
supporting_citation: Hamosh A, Scott AF, Amberger JS, Bocchini CA, McKusick VA. Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM), a knowledgebase of human genes and genetic disorders. Nucleic Acids Res. 2005;33(Database issue):D514-D517. doi:10.1093/nar/gki033.

primary_purpose: Assessment of gene–disease validity and clinical relevance
output: Rare disease and gene association context
selection_rationale: Included for rare-disease nomenclature and gene–disease context.
appropriate_use: Use when rare-disease terminology and cross-referenced disease context are needed.
interpretation_boundary: Does not independently establish causality in an individual case.
key_limitations: Evidence is evolving and may vary in strength and curation status.
supporting_citation: Rath A, Olry A, Dhombres F, Brandt MM, Urbero B, Ayme S. Representation of rare diseases in health information systems: the Orphanet approach to serve a wide range of end users. Hum Mutat. 2012;33(5):803-808. doi:10.1002/humu.22078.

primary_purpose: Assessment of gene–disease validity and clinical relevance
selection_rationale: Included because diagnostic panel curation can provide disease-specific gene relevance context.
appropriate_use: Use as a complementary source when panel evidence and panel scope are relevant.
interpretation_boundary: Panel inclusion is not synonymous with definitive causality or variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Evidence is evolving and may vary in strength and curation status. Panel content and evidence ratings change; jurisdiction-specific practices may differ.
supporting_citation: Martin AR, Williams E, Foulger RE, Leigh S, Daugherty LC, Niblock O, et al. PanelApp crowdsources expert knowledge to establish consensus diagnostic gene panels. Nat Genet. 2019;51(11):1560-1565. doi:10.1038/s41588-019-0528-2.

primary_purpose: Prediction of potential functional effects
selection_rationale: Included as a representative broad variant-effect predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as one supportive computational feature when applicable to the variant class.
interpretation_boundary: Score alone is not clinical pathogenicity evidence.
key_limitations: Model-dependent performance and applicability across variant types and populations.
supporting_citation: Rentzsch P, Witten D, Cooper GM, Shendure J, Kircher M. CADD: predicting the deleteriousness of variants throughout the human genome. Nucleic Acids Res. 2019;47(D1):D886-D894. doi:10.1093/nar/gky1016.

primary_purpose: Prediction of potential functional effects
selection_rationale: Included as a representative ensemble predictor for missense variants.
appropriate_use: Use only for applicable missense variants and with gene/disease mechanism context.
interpretation_boundary: Do not treat concordance with related predictors as independent evidence.
key_limitations: Model-dependent performance and applicability across variant types and populations. Training-data overlap, calibration, and gene- and variant-specific performance limitations.
supporting_citation: Ioannidis NM, Rothstein JH, Pejaver V, Middha S, McDonnell SK, Baheti S, et al. REVEL: an ensemble method for predicting the pathogenicity of rare missense variants. Am J Hum Genet. 2016;99(4):877-885. doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.08.016.

primary_purpose: Prediction of potential functional effects
technical_compatibility: Protein/variant input. Genome build is inherited from the annotation implementation.
selection_rationale: Included as a commonly used conservation/function-based missense predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as one supporting predictor for applicable missense variants.
interpretation_boundary: Not a stand-alone clinical classification method.
key_limitations: Model-dependent performance and applicability across variant types and populations. The public website returned an error on a 2026-10-10 check.
supporting_citation: Ng PC, Henikoff S. SIFT: predicting amino acid changes that affect protein function. Nucleic Acids Res. 2003;31(13):3812-3814. doi:10.1093/nar/gkg509.

primary_purpose: Prediction of potential functional effects
technical_compatibility: Protein/variant input. Genome build is inherited from the annotation implementation.
selection_rationale: Included as a historical and commonly used missense-effect predictor.
appropriate_use: Use as supportive context for applicable missense variants.
interpretation_boundary: Not independent confirmation when used with overlapping predictors.
key_limitations: Model-dependent performance and applicability across variant types and populations. Limited clinical specificity.
supporting_citation: Adzhubei IA, Schmidt S, Peshkin L, Ramensky VE, Gerasimova A, Bork P, et al. A method and server for predicting damaging missense mutations. Nat Methods. 2010;7(4):248-249. doi:10.1038/nmeth0410-248.

primary_purpose: Prediction of potential functional effects
technical_compatibility: Protein or transcript input. The catalogued URL is a public browser of the AlphaMissense score set (Cheng et al. 2023), which is separate from AlphaFold DB.
selection_rationale: Included as a modern missense-focused predictor that may add complementary computational context.
appropriate_use: Use for applicable missense variants with explicit transcript/protein mapping.
interpretation_boundary: Do not use as autonomous clinical classification evidence.
key_limitations: Model-dependent performance and applicability across variant types and populations.
supporting_citation: Cheng J, Novati G, Pan J, Bycroft C, Žemgulytė A, Applebaum T, et al. Accurate proteome-wide missense variant effect prediction with AlphaMissense. Science. 2023;382(6673):eadg7492. doi:10.1126/science.adg7492.

primary_purpose: Assessment of potential splicing effects
output: Splice alteration delta scores and positions
selection_rationale: Included as a representative splice-effect predictor for variants with plausible splicing consequences.
appropriate_use: Use with explicit transcript selection and consideration of relevant splice mechanisms.
interpretation_boundary: Prediction is not direct proof of aberrant splicing or clinical pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Tissue, transcript, and context dependence.
supporting_citation: Jaganathan K, Kyriazopoulou Panagiotopoulou S, McRae JF, Darbandi SF, Knowles D, Li YI, et al. Predicting splicing from primary sequence with deep learning. Cell. 2019;176(3):535-548.e24. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2018.12.015.

primary_purpose: Assessment of potential splicing effects
technical_compatibility: Sequence-based input. Build is implied by the sequence context supplied to the scorer. The original Burge-lab score scripts have been intermittently unavailable; this entry cites the method paper.
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary sequence-based splicing assessment method.
appropriate_use: Use for relevant canonical or near-canonical splice-site questions.
interpretation_boundary: Does not demonstrate in vivo splicing outcome.
key_limitations: Tissue, transcript, and context dependence.
supporting_citation: Yeo G, Burge CB. Maximum entropy modeling of short sequence motifs with applications to RNA splicing signals. J Comput Biol. 2004;11(2-3):377-394. doi:10.1089/1066527041410418.

primary_purpose: Assessment of potential splicing effects
technical_compatibility: Database/annotation integration. v1.1 contains GRCh37 coordinates and GRCh38 coordinates lifted from GRCh37.
selection_rationale: Included as a supplementary source of precomputed splicing prediction context.
appropriate_use: Use as complementary computational information for applicable SNVs.
interpretation_boundary: Not direct experimental evidence of aberrant splicing.
key_limitations: Tissue, transcript, and context dependence. The scored set is the frozen v1.1 release and is limited to consensus-region SNVs. Distribution through dbNSFP does not make dbNSFP this resource.
supporting_citation: Jian X, Boerwinkle E, Liu X. In silico prediction of splice-altering single nucleotide variants in the human genome. Nucleic Acids Res. 2014;42(22):13534-13544. doi:10.1093/nar/gku1206.

primary_purpose: Assessment of regulatory and expression-related evidence
technical_compatibility: Web/API/data downloads. Which builds are available depends on the resource release.
selection_rationale: Included because tissue-specific expression context can inform biological plausibility and regulatory interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when relevant tissues and biological context are available.
interpretation_boundary: Expression context does not independently establish variant pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Tissue specificity and incomplete functional annotation. Donor composition, tissue availability, and association limitations.
supporting_citation: GTEx Consortium. The GTEx Consortium atlas of genetic regulatory effects across human tissues. Science. 2020;369(6509):1318-1330. doi:10.1126/science.aaz1776.

primary_purpose: Assessment of regulatory and expression-related evidence
selection_rationale: Included for experimentally derived functional-genomic context around noncoding or regulatory variants.
appropriate_use: Use when genomic coordinates overlap relevant regulatory annotations.
interpretation_boundary: Annotation overlap does not prove disease mechanism or clinical impact.
key_limitations: Tissue specificity and incomplete functional annotation. Cell-type and experimental-context specificity; incomplete coverage.
supporting_citation: ENCODE Project Consortium. An integrated encyclopedia of DNA elements in the human genome. Nature. 2012;489(7414):57-74. doi:10.1038/nature11247.

primary_purpose: Assessment of regulatory and expression-related evidence
selection_rationale: Included as an integrative entry point for regulatory annotation.
appropriate_use: Use for hypothesis generation regarding regulatory context.
interpretation_boundary: Scores are not direct clinical pathogenicity evidence.
key_limitations: Tissue specificity and incomplete functional annotation.
supporting_citation: Boyle AP, Hong EL, Hariharan M, Cheng Y, Schaub MA, Kasowski M, et al. Annotation of functional variation in personal genomes using RegulomeDB. Genome Res. 2012;22(9):1790-1797. doi:10.1101/gr.137323.112.

primary_purpose: Assessment of regulatory and expression-related evidence
selection_rationale: Included as a complementary functional-genomics resource for promoter/enhancer and expression context.
appropriate_use: Use when relevant cell-type or regulatory annotation is needed.
interpretation_boundary: Does not by itself establish variant effect or causality.
key_limitations: Tissue specificity and incomplete functional annotation. Update status must be checked.
supporting_citation: Forrest ARR, Kawaji H, Rehli M, Baillie JK, de Hoon MJL, Haberle V, et al. A promoter-level mammalian expression atlas. Nature. 2014;507(7493):462-470. doi:10.1038/nature13182.

primary_purpose: Assessment of protein structure and function
selection_rationale: Included for curated protein-function and domain context relevant to variant interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when a variant can be mapped reliably to a protein sequence and functional feature.
interpretation_boundary: Protein annotation alone does not determine clinical significance.
key_limitations: Structural prediction and functional uncertainty. Annotation completeness and isoform mapping can vary.
supporting_citation: UniProt Consortium. UniProt: the Universal Protein Knowledgebase in 2023. Nucleic Acids Res. 2023;51(D1):D523-D531. doi:10.1093/nar/gkac1052.

primary_purpose: Assessment of protein structure and function
selection_rationale: Included where experimentally resolved structure can inform residue-level or domain-level context.
appropriate_use: Use when reliable structural coverage and mapping are available.
interpretation_boundary: Structure presence does not prove functional or clinical impact.
key_limitations: Structural prediction and functional uncertainty. Incomplete protein coverage; construct and experimental context limitations.
supporting_citation: wwPDB Consortium. Protein Data Bank: the single global archive for 3D macromolecular structure data. Nucleic Acids Res. 2019;47(D1):D520-D528. doi:10.1093/nar/gky949.

primary_purpose: Assessment of protein structure and function
selection_rationale: Included for structural hypothesis generation when experimental structures are unavailable.
appropriate_use: Use with confidence measures and in conjunction with known protein biology.
interpretation_boundary: Predicted structure is not direct functional or clinical evidence.
key_limitations: Structural prediction and functional uncertainty. Prediction confidence, conformational dynamics, complexes, and mapping limitations.
supporting_citation: Varadi M, Anyango S, Deshpande M, Nair S, Natassia C, Yordanova G, et al. AlphaFold Protein Structure Database: massively expanding the structural coverage of protein-sequence space with high-accuracy models. Nucleic Acids Res. 2022;50(D1):D439-D444. doi:10.1093/nar/gkab1061.

primary_purpose: Assessment of protein structure and function
selection_rationale: Included for standardized domain and family context during protein-level interpretation.
appropriate_use: Use when variant localization relative to known domains is relevant.
interpretation_boundary: Domain overlap alone does not establish pathogenicity.
key_limitations: Structural prediction and functional uncertainty. Annotation coverage and functional specificity vary.
supporting_citation: Paysan-Lafosse T, Blum M, Chuguransky S, Grego T, Pinto BL, Salazar GA, et al. InterPro in 2022. Nucleic Acids Res. 2023;51(D1):D418-D427. doi:10.1093/nar/gkac993.

primary_purpose: Computational support for variant and gene prioritization
input: Phenotype, gene, and variant queries related to mitochondrial disease
output: Mitochondrial-disease knowledge retrieval and prioritization context
selection_rationale: Retired from the core representative set. MSeqDR-QM is not listed among the representative resources in Table 1. Mitochondrial variants are outside the scope of the framework.
appropriate_use: Not used in the current representative mapping. Retained so an earlier citation of this entry can be traced.
interpretation_boundary: A mitochondrial-disease query result does not establish causality and is not a classification.
key_limitations: Bias, interpretability, model dependence, and variable validation. Mitochondrial variants are outside the scope of the framework.
supporting_citation: Not cited among the representative resources in the manuscript. Mitochondrial variants are outside the framework scope.

primary_purpose: Computational support for variant and gene prioritization
technical_compatibility: Web platform; VCF and optional pedigree or control inputs. The public site is served over HTTP.
selection_rationale: Included as a representative cloud workflow that can filter and prioritize germline variants from a VCF using a saved recipe. Use across stages 5–9 is context dependent. Component databases and predictors still have to be appraised on their own.
appropriate_use: Use when the documented inputs, recipe, and version fit the case, including optional pedigree or control files.
interpretation_boundary: A prioritized list does not establish gene–disease validity, a splice effect, or a clinical classification.
key_limitations: Bias, interpretability, model dependence, and variable validation. Results depend on the selected filters, predictor thresholds, and embedded data releases. Concordance among embedded predictors is not independent evidence.
supporting_citation: Chen S, Francioli LC, Goodrich JK, Collins RL, Kanai M, Wang Q, et al. GeMSTONE: orchestrated prioritization of human germline mutations in the cloud. Nucleic Acids Res. 2017;45(W1):W207-W214. doi:10.1093/nar/gkx398.

primary_purpose: Retrieval and assessment of clinical and literature-based evidence; Clinical reporting, documentation, and reassessment
output: Clinical significance submissions, review status, conflicts
selection_rationale: Included to retrieve prior clinical assertions, review status, conflicts, and associated evidence context.
appropriate_use: Use when reviewing previously reported clinical interpretations.
interpretation_boundary: Entries are not definitive conclusions and must be appraised in context.
key_limitations: Conflicting, heterogeneous, or incompletely curated evidence. Evidence and interpretations may change over time.
supporting_citation: Landrum MJ, Lee JM, Benson M, Brown G, Chao C, Chitipiralla S, et al. ClinVar: improving access to variant interpretations and supporting evidence. Nucleic Acids Res. 2018;46(D1):D1062-D1067. doi:10.1093/nar/gkx1153.

primary_purpose: Retrieval and assessment of clinical and literature-based evidence
selection_rationale: Included as a literature-derived variant resource that may support evidence retrieval where access is available.
appropriate_use: Use as a starting point for primary-literature verification.
interpretation_boundary: A reported disease association is not a final classification.
key_limitations: Conflicting, heterogeneous, or incompletely curated evidence. Subscription access, curation criteria, and need for primary-source appraisal.
supporting_citation: Stenson PD, Mort M, Ball EV, Chapman M, Evans K, Azevedo L, et al. The Human Gene Mutation Database (HGMD): optimizing its use in a clinical diagnostic or research setting. Hum Genet. 2020;139(10):1197-1207. doi:10.1007/s00439-020-02199-3.

primary_purpose: Retrieval and assessment of clinical and literature-based evidence
output: Literature links and indexed evidence context
technical_compatibility: Web platform; query based. Coordinate queries depend on the build used for variant normalization.
selection_rationale: Included to support efficient retrieval of relevant published evidence.
appropriate_use: Use to identify literature for direct appraisal.
interpretation_boundary: Search results do not replace assessment of study quality or applicability.
key_limitations: Conflicting, heterogeneous, or incompletely curated evidence. Indexing scope, access tier, normalization, and literature quality vary.
supporting_citation: Chunn LM, Nefcy DC, Scouten RW, Tarpey RP, Chauhan G, Lim MS, et al. Mastermind: a comprehensive genomic association search engine for empirical evidence curation and genetic variant interpretation. Front Genet. 2020;11:577152. doi:10.3389/fgene.2020.577152.

primary_purpose: Retrieval and assessment of clinical and literature-based evidence
output: Bibliographic records and links to literature
selection_rationale: Included as a core bibliographic source for retrieving primary studies, guidelines, and resource documentation.
appropriate_use: Use for direct appraisal of source evidence.
interpretation_boundary: Search retrieval is not evidence appraisal or clinical classification.
key_limitations: Conflicting, heterogeneous, or incompletely curated evidence. Indexing, query design, publication bias, and access limitations.
supporting_citation: Sayers EW, Cavanaugh M, Clark K, Pruitt KD, Schoch CL, Sherry ST, et al. Database resources of the National Center for Biotechnology Information in 2025. Nucleic Acids Res. 2025;53(D1):D20-D29. doi:10.1093/nar/gkae979.

primary_purpose: Clinical variant classification using ACMG/AMP criteria
selection_rationale: Retired from the core representative set. Table 1 lists InterVar, VarSome, Franklin, and ClinGen specifications for ACMG/AMP classification. Richards et al. 2015 remains the classification standard cited by the framework.
appropriate_use: Not a selected resource in the ACMG/AMP classification row. The criteria remain the standard applied at clinical variant classification.
interpretation_boundary: Criteria do not replace evidence quality review, clinical context, or expert judgment.
key_limitations: Requires contextual assessment and expert review.
supporting_citation: Richards S, Aziz N, Bale S, Bick D, Das S, Gastier-Foster J, et al. Standards and guidelines for the interpretation and reporting of sequence variants: a joint consensus recommendation of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology. Genet Med. 2015;17(5):405-424. doi:10.1038/gim.2015.30.

primary_purpose: Clinical variant classification using ACMG/AMP criteria
selection_rationale: Included because applicable expert specifications can improve consistency of ACMG/AMP criteria application.
